original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The binding affinity of HUP-46, KYP-2091, and KYP-2112 to human wild-type PREP was assessed by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) as described previously.17,32 Briefly, the experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (10 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand (100 μM) was loaded into the syringe. The buffer used was 20 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.4) containing 150 mM NaCl. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA, U.S.A.) with a one-site binding model. The binding constant (Kd) was calculated from the binding isotherm. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the results are presented as mean ± SEM.
